Explore a management planning example

A sale can close before the customer pays.

Compare when deals may close with when payments may arrive. Choose 30, 60 or 90 days. All figures are fictional Jamaican dollars, not AyudaGrow results or customer financial data.

Sales forecastJ$350,000Deals closing within 30 days
Cash receipt forecastJ$50,000Payments arriving within 30 days

Illustrative, probability-weighted estimates. Both totals use deal value x assumed chance of winning. Neither is confirmed sales or money already received.

Why is the cash estimate J$300,000 lower?

The office equipment proposal adds J$300,000 to the sales forecast (J$400,000 x a 75% assumed chance of winning). The sale is assumed to close on day 20, but payment is assumed on day 50, outside this 30-day window.

Before planning spending, check when customers may pay.

Each horizon starts today. The 60-day figure includes the first 30 days; do not add the three figures together. This teaching model is not a replica of a configured product dashboard.

See the sample records and calculation assumptions

For this illustration only, weighted value = opportunity value x an assumed probability. Sales enter the view by the expected close day; potential receipts use a separate assumed payment day. The same weighting is used for receipts solely to explain the timing difference, not to predict individual customer payments.

From dashboard to decision

The number is the start.
The next action matters.

Use a shared view to ask better questions before making commitments. In this example, a Jamaican supplier reviews the pipeline with the team at the start of the week.

01 / FOLLOW-UP

A J$300,000 proposal has gone quiet.

THE SIGNAL

The record shows no activity in eight days.

THE MANAGEMENT RESPONSE

Ask the account manager to check the buyer's status, record the next step and revise the expected close date if needed.

02 / STAFFING

Possible work is building for the next quarter.

THE SIGNAL

The 90-day weighted sales estimate is J$600,000.

THE MANAGEMENT RESPONSE

Review delivery dates and team capacity. Explore staffing options alongside signed work and downside scenarios before making a hiring commitment.

03 / PURCHASING

Expected sales arrive before some payments.

THE SIGNAL

By day 30, estimated sales are J$350,000 but potential receipts are J$50,000.

THE MANAGEMENT RESPONSE

Check deposits, supplier terms and existing cash before ordering stock. A likely sale does not fund a purchase until cash is available.

04 / TARGETS

The outlook is below the planning target.

THE SIGNAL

J$600,000 expected against a fictional J$700,000 90-day sales target leaves a J$100,000 gap.

THE MANAGEMENT RESPONSE

Review conversion, slipping deals and new opportunities. Adjust the plan rather than treating the target as a promised result.

Better records. More useful conversations.

A forecast is only as useful as its inputs.

Keep opportunity values, owners, stages, probabilities and expected dates current. Agree what the numbers mean and review the underlying deals, not just the chart.

For potential cash inflows, payment terms and receipt timing matter too. If those details are missing, show the gap instead of presenting a precise-looking answer.

Explore the CRM foundation 
  1. DefineAgree stages, values, reporting periods and what counts as a conversion.
  2. MaintainUpdate close dates and next actions. Remove duplicate or no-longer-active opportunities.
  3. CompareReview forecast versus actual outcomes and understand where assumptions were wrong.
  4. ActAssign follow-up, revisit probabilities and bring meaningful changes into the next review.
A wider view of performance

Know what is happening.
Learn what is working.

Choose reports that answer a real management question, using the data your team actually captures.

Pipeline & opportunity value

Review stages, owners and amounts. Separate total open value from weighted expectations and won opportunities.

Conversion & lead sources

Compare how enquiries progress by source and stage. Use consistent definitions and complete attribution before deciding which channels work best.

Appointments & activity

Review bookings, attendance and follow-through where these are captured and configured. Identify gaps in the process before blaming the people.

Selected planning periods

Agree useful horizons, such as 30, 60 and 90 days, where the configured reports and data support them. Use date filters and source records consistently.

Know the limits before you rely on the view

Planning support.
Not a financial guarantee.

Forecasts are estimates based on available CRM and sales information. They are not audited accounting projections, guaranteed revenue, guaranteed cash flow or a substitute for your financial records and professional judgment.

The 30/60/90-day cash-inflow illustration requires receipt-timing assumptions beyond a sales close date. A ready-made cash forecast, bank integration or accounting integration is not promised here. Confirm the available data, calculation method, reports and any additional configuration before activation.

Opportunity forecasting can use time-based views and weighted values. Account availability, settings and exact calculations still need verification for your setup.
